title: Diagram Evaluation Study
difficultyNote: Difficulty is structural complexity from a visual review (diagrams/human_study). Shown to researchers only.

diagrams.caption: Flow diagram of the study design, from participant selection to the data included in this open dataset. Of 200 recruited and assessed for eligibility, 8 are excluded (no consent for data publishing), and 192 included in the dataset complete genetic screening, psychometric tests, health, and demographic questionnaires. Participants allocation for neuroimaging and blood tests (N = 79) then branches into fMRI (N = 69, after exclusions), EEG (N = 79), and Blood tests (N = 77, after withdrawals).

Flow chart of patient enrollment, with exclusions listed on the side. From 604 patients with high probability for choledocholithiasis, those with malignant biliary obstruction or altered GI anatomy are excluded (297 non cancer patients), then those whose initial abdominal CT scan revealed choledocholithiasis (127 with negative CT scan), then delayed ERCP cases. The rest split into EUS-first attempt (N=44) and ERCP-first attempt (N=64), yielding the EUS-first group (N=44) and ERCP-first group (N=60), followed by Follow-up 3 months.

Case selection flow chart for chest examinations of patients with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). From 10522 examinations of the chest, 9971 are excluded, leaving 551 COVID-19 related examinations of the chest. These split into 181 examinations of outpatients (20 chest CTs and 161 chest x-rays) and 370 examinations of in-patients (62 chest CTs and 308 chest x-rays).

Flowchart of research objects. Neonates from local CHCs undergo Candidates identification (No: Not study objects; Yes: n=18983), then Ultrasound in Minhang MCH, which separates normal or other abnormalities from RPD (renal pelvis dilatation, n=2392). At Meet referral criteria?, Yes leads to Further examination, diagnosis and intervention in CHFU (n=47), and No leads to Follow-up in Minhang MCH (n=1409), which ends in meet referral criteria (feeding back to CHFU), Mid-term termination of follow-up, or Normal termination of follow-up.

Flowchart of defining cases and controls among migraine patients from an EHR database. Patients meeting exclusion criteria (coexistent brain disorders, age < 18) are Excluded; the rest pass sequential Migraine with aura, Migraine without aura, and Unclassified migraine decisions, each requiring enough codes in at least two encounters, yielding three migraine case groups, with unclassifiable patients excluded. A Stroke decision excludes stroke diagnosed before migraine and divides patients into Hemorrhagic stroke cases, Ischemic stroke cases, and Controls (stroke-free migraine patients).

Workflow for reconstructing CT and spectral images using the proposed dataset. High and Total Energy Counting Projections pass through Correction and Reconstruction to produce Low, High, Total CT Images. Spectral Reconstruction of these images then yields a group of outputs: Basis Material Images, Virtual Monoenergetic Images, and further images indicated by an ellipsis.

Proposed workflow for applying the TGx-DDI biomarker for genotoxicity assessment. In (A), a Drug Candidate tested under ICH S2(R1) Option 1 (AMES negative, In vitro chromosome damage positive, In vivo micronucleus negative) yields TGx-DDI Results feeding a WoE Assessment judged Relevant or Irrelevant. In (B), a Chemical tested by TGx-DDI (probability analysis, 2D clustering, principle component analysis) gets an overall positive or negative DDI call informing Hazard ID, Mode of Action and Weight of Evidence assessment, and Potency assessment.

General overview of the HC4N strategy, arranged along an axis of increasing protein similarity level. The whole IP dataset (level 0) is analyzed with 4N to give possibly overlapping clusters (level 1). The proteins of each cluster form IP subsets, and 4N on each subset gives level 2 clusters; repeating this on IP sub-subsets gives level 3. A legend distinguishes clusters that are leaf nodes, inner nodes, and overlapping clusters sharing proteins.

Flowchart of the number of participants included in the analysis from 2006 to 2016. It starts with 18,465 eligible participants with data on wealth and education in 2006; after excluding those lost to follow-up, 14,627 with data on behaviours remain in 2010. Excluding further losses and those with no data on Allostatic Load leaves 4100 in 2012, and after losses to follow-up between 2012 and 2016, 3336 participants are included in the analysis.

CONSORT diagram of the PRACTICAL trial of remote urinary incontinence (UI) treatments. Of 2082 assessed for eligibility, 292 consent and 286 are randomized to UI app (147) or video visit (139). In each arm, the 8-wk Assessment classifies participants as Responder (minimal clinically important difference, MCID ≥2.52) or Nonresponder (MCID <2.52); nonresponders either continue their assigned treatment or receive a Video visit booster. All paths then merge for analysis of 12-wk and 24-wk outcomes.

Flowchart of treatment and outcomes for adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secreting pituitary adenomas (N=4). The tumors split into Macroadenomas (N=1), treated by Surgery and ending in hormonal control and no visible tumor, and Microadenomas (N=3), treated by surgery, surgery+medication+bilateral adrenalectomy, or medication (N=1 each). Microadenoma outcomes are hormonal control (N=3), no visible tumor (N=2), and size stable (N=1).

PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) flowchart organized into Identification, Screening, Eligibility, and Included phases. Records identified through database searching (n = 1894) fall to 1871 after duplicates removed; of the records screened, 1843 are excluded. Of 28 full-text articles assessed for eligibility, some are excluded for listed reasons (lack comparison group, did not report required outcomes, review articles, others), leaving 14 studies included.

Flowchart of reported pediatric COVID-19 cases with COVID-19-related hospitalization, ICU admission and death from July to October 2021. It starts from children ≤17 years of age in Germany, then children with SARS-CoV-2 IgG positivity, case reporting to registries in German children's hospitals, and hospitalization associated with SARS-CoV-2. Hospitalizations split into <5, 5-11, and 12-17 years old, each leading to COVID-19 requiring treatment and ICU admission, with lines from all three age groups converging on Death (nS = 9).

BDT of the reduced model showing decisions in input variables that cause bifurcations and affect attractor phenotypes. The root splits on Viral_dsRNA_rna_reduced (virus replication detection), and each branch then splits on GRL0617_drug, leading to either an Nsp15 split or an Azithromycin_drug split followed by further Nsp15 splits. Leaves show attractor outcomes or Mixed Phenotype nodes (3, 4, or 2 types), and decisions marked (1)–(3) are those significant for the IIR phenotypes.

Flow chart for selecting the participants according to the OSTA risk level. From 3,104 women aged ≥ 45 years old who underwent spirometry and DXA, those pre-menopausal, using medication for osteoporosis, or with thyroid or chronic kidney disease are excluded, leaving 1,770 participants. Excluding respiratory conditions (asthma, tuberculosis or pleurisy, bronchiectasis, lung cancer, other respiratory disease) and abnormal FEV1 values leaves 1,580 participants, divided into OSTA low risk (645), moderate risk (752), and high risk (183).

Patients flow chart. Of 192 patients suspected with coronary artery disease (CAD), 19 are excluded for angiography image loss, LVEF ≤ 50%, or missing target vessel information, leaving 173 who underwent invasive coronary angiography (ICA) and wire-based index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) measurement. After 34 more exclusions for poor contrast opacification, projections separated by <25°, or severe overlap or distortion, 139 patients (involving 201 vessels) finished CAG-IMR measurement.

Flow chart of participants in the study. The total of 63 participants splits into a Silence condition (N=26) and a Noise condition (N=37). Each condition is further divided into Non-habituated and Habituated participants: 2 and 24 in the silence condition, and 13 and 24 in the noise condition.

Flowchart of patient selection for training, validation, and test datasets. From 872 Appendicitis CTs (2011–2020), exclusions (age < 20, duplicate patient, perforation, unclear appendix location, appendix tumor identified) leave 567; 50 are randomly selected for validation and 517 form the Training dataset. These 50 join 50 Control CTs performed for acute abdomen to form the Validation dataset (n = 100). Similarly, 100 Appendicitis CTs and 100 Control CTs after 1/1/2021 form the Test dataset (n = 200).

Flowchart of participant enrolment and study progression in a trial of SAFETY (Safe Alternatives for Teens and Youths). Of 53 referrals, 15 are excluded and 38 are assessed for eligibility; after 8 more exclusions, 30 are randomized to SAFETY treatment 12 weeks (n = 15) or Supportive Therapy treatment 12 weeks (n = 15). Each arm proceeds through Post-treatment and 3-month post-treatment assessments to an Intention-to-treat analysis (n = 15).

Flow chart of individuals in Belgium fully vaccinated for at least 14 days and their breakthrough COVID-19 infections. Of 8,062,600 individuals aged ≥18 fully vaccinated between 1 February and 5 December 2021, 373,070 have breakthrough infections (4.6%). After excluding 156,256 without information on symptoms, 216,814 breakthrough infections with information on symptoms remain, of which 151,888 are symptomatic (70.1%) and 64,926 asymptomatic (29.9%).

Flow chart of the literature identification and screening process via databases and ancestral search, organized into Identification, Screening, and Included phases. Records identified from Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and Academic Premier (n = 826) lose 335 duplicates before screening. Of 491 records screened, 346 are excluded, and of 145 reports assessed for eligibility, 130 are excluded; Ancestral Searching (n = 5) then leads to 20 studies included in review.

Flow chart of enrolled patients in the study. Of 561 esophageal cancer patients who had undergone contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) between January 2017 and February 2019, 343 patients with ESCC meet the inclusion criteria, such as confirmed ESCC with definite LVI status after radical resection. After exclusion criteria (antitumor treatment before surgery, multiple tumors, unidentifiable lesions, artefacts), 224 eligible patients are included and divided into a Training set (n=158) and a Testing set (n=66).

Adaptive Management Cycle with double-loop learning. In the deliberative phase, Assess problem leads to Design and then Implement; in the iterative phase, Monitor leads to Evaluate and then Adjust. From Adjust, a single loop (adjusting decisions based on technical learning) returns to Monitor, while a double loop (reformulating the decision architecture based on technical and institutional learning) returns to Assess problem, closing the cycle.

Process flow diagram of circRNA vaccine production in four stages. Plasmid linearization runs from Design the sequence through recombinant plasmid building, transformation and bacteria proliferation, plasmid extraction, and enzyme digestion to linear plasmid purification. RNA circularization covers in vitro transcription, RNA purification, circularization by group I/II intron or T4 RNA ligase, and circular RNA purification. Encapsulation by lipid nanoparticles or other delivery systems and Filtration precede Fill-to-finish manufacturing: filling into containers, capping, sealing, and labeling and packaging.

Patient selection flowchart for the training dataset based on VFSS data quality. From 2343 cases, 456 clear cases are rated Quality 1, reduced to 309 after excluding 147 cases due to incomplete study or long study time. The next 1885 cases yield 758 with severe oral phase delay or transparent airway intubation (Quality 2), the next 1127 yield 243 with severe oral phase delay, airway intubation, or artifact like necklace (Quality 3), and 884 unidentifiable cases are Quality 4.

Flow diagram of evaluations of talaromycosis in children with IEI. Of 329 patients with talaromycosis from 2012 to 2024, exclusions for age > 14, lacking WES test, and lacking clinical data leave 18 children with complete clinical data and WES test. These split into novel IEI genetic defects (n=5; IL7R, LYST, PLCG2, DOCK8, KRAS) and reported IEI genetic defects (n=13; STAT1, IL2RG, CD40L, STAT3, CARD9), followed through induction phase, maintenance phase, and long time follow-up, ending with 10/18 confirmed alive.

CONSORT flow diagram of participant enrollment, randomization, follow-up, and analysis. Enrollment proceeds from subject selection (n = 60) to checking general health and completing consent forms, then measurement of anthropometric data. At allocation, after a pre-test, subjects are randomized into six groups of 10: CON, USRPT, PLA+USRPT, PRO+USRPT, OMEGA+USRPT, and PRO+OMEGA+USRPT, each with its own protocol. All groups converge on a post-test after eight weeks (n=60), followed by data analysis.

Flowchart of the inclusion of mammographic screening examinations. 2,610 diagnosed cancers split into 1,916 screen detected cancers and 694 interval cancers; after exclusions such as not invasive or not all images available, 768 screen detected and 411 interval cancers remain. Each arm is divided into mass visible and no mass visible, and after calculating masking risk, cases are grouped as low versus high masking risk (Analysis 1) and as low, unknown, intermediate, and high masking risk (Analysis 2).

Decision tree and Markov model for estimating the cost-effectiveness of screening for HTN. (A) In the single-screening tree, normal and hypertension cohorts receive screening or no screening; results are true/false positive or negative, and hypertension leads to treatment (controlled or uncontrolled) or no treatment, each ending in a Markov node. (B) A 2nd screening or no 2nd screening follows a positive first result. (C) Markov states run from Healthy to HTN to MI, stroke, CKD, or heart failure, then Death.

Flowchart of patient inclusion, allocation, and follow-up. Sixty patients were enrolled and randomised, with 30 assigned to the probiotic group and 30 to the placebo group. In the probiotic group, 6 discontinued (2 started immunotherapy, 1 had nausea, 3 by own decision), leaving 24 who completed the trial; in the placebo group, 14 discontinued (1 had abdominal pain, 2 had pruritic episodes, 11 by own decision), leaving 16 who completed the trial.

Workflow for screening carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) and vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) from inpatient rectal swabs, in two parallel arms. The pooling samples + Xpert Assay arm splits into positive and negative pools, which are compared with cultures to give true positive, false positive, true negative, and false negative results. The cultures + MALDI-TOF MS arm sends CPE and VRE culture-positive isolates to Xpert Carba-R and Xpert-vanA/B, respectively, each yielding negative or positive results.

Flow chart showing number (%) of participations in the primary outcome measurements in 2006 and 2008. Six elementary schools in Reykjavik (N=321) undergo cluster randomization into 3 intervention schools (N=151) and 3 control schools (N=170) of children attending 2nd class in fall 2006. After children who refused or were absent at baseline are removed (22 and 30), a table gives participation in 2006, 2008, and both years for blood tests, blood pressure, DXA scans, and fitness tests.

Flow chart of WES and transcriptome data processing. The DNA arm pre-processes whole exome sequencing reads (mapping to GRCh37.p13+mm10, duplicate marking, human/mouse read splitting, realignment, recalibration), then performs variants calling, filtering, annotation, second filtering, and cancer related 381 genes filtering, yielding total and cancer related somatic mutations. The RNA arm pre-processes mRNA sequencing (mapping, read counting, normalization by FPKM), then branches into hierarchical clustering and DEG analysis, where up- and down-regulated genes undergo ontology analysis.

Flow chart of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) patient follow-up. COPD patients randomly selected from 56 primary health care centres (PHCCs) and 14 hospitals (N = 1,548) narrow to 1,111 who consented to questionnaires and record review, then 970 with completed Clinical COPD Questionnaire (CCQ) forms in 2005. After removing deceased patients and those with no present address, 692 received a follow-up questionnaire in 2012, 501 returned it, and 413 had completed CCQ forms in 2012.

Consort flow chart showing how the analytical sample was derived from the patients who were assessed for eligibility. Of 184 acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients with recent/current pulmonary function tests (PFTs) assessed (STEMI and NSTEMI), 75 were excluded for no adequate post-AMI transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE). The 109 enrolled patients (41 STEMI, 68 NSTEMI) were then divided into COPD (n = 45) and non-COPD (n = 64) groups.

Flowchart describing the logic of the RIA procedure, where P is the number of scale items to distribute. It starts by choosing P_X << P, then randomly allocates P_X items to the X-Block, and finally randomly divides the remaining (P − P_X) items among the A-, B-, and C-Blocks.

Common collision avoidance pipeline based on the MPPI algorithm, adapted for decentralized multi-agent scenarios. Actuators act on the environment, which returns the agent state and neighbors states to MPPI, alongside parameters μ, Σ, T, K. Inside MPPI, neighbors states feed ORCA linear constraints and neighbors trajectories prediction; the asterisked step computes μ′, Σ′ from ORCA lines for t = 0 to seed control/trajectory sampling of K samples. Trajectories weights are computed, and control based on weights goes to the actuators.

Procedure of obtaining patients for the study, Alert Hospital, 2016–2021. Of 443 MDR TB patients enrolled from 2016-2021, patients excluded were those who discontinued TB treatment (5) or had missing information (3), leaving a final sample of 435.

Flowchart of a general machine learning pipeline to process acoustic/prosodic correlates of disease, adapted from Braga et al. [31]. In training, recordings undergo feature extraction and normalization and, with metadata, fill a database split into training and validation subsets; model training yields a candidate data model whose estimated classification undergoes performance evaluation, looping back through optimization. At run-time, a new recording passes through feature extraction and the optimized data model, producing an Alzheimer's Disease classification estimate.

Decision scheme on transmission pattern for countries in the WHO African region. It first asks how many COVID-19 cases occurred in the past 28 days; zero cases leads to No Cases. Otherwise, mostly imported cases in the last 14 days give Sporadic Cases, while locally transmitted cases with at least 80% linked to a confirmed case (Yes) give Clusters of Cases. If No, cases/million in the past 14 days define community transmission with low, moderate, high, or uncontrolled incidence.

Flow diagram illustrating the participant selection process. Starting from 50,965 participants from NHANES 2005-2014, excluding those aged <20 or pregnant leaves 27,909. Excluding those with missing dietary or sleep questionnaire data or unknown survival data leaves 24,929, and excluding those missing other covariates (such as PIR, BMI, drinking, and PHQ9) yields the final 21,233.

Adapted allocation guidelines for referral decisions after detoxifications. At treatment intake, three criteria (physical condition, psychiatric condition, crisis intervention) are reviewed, and the allocation guidelines are used only if none is met. Recommendations draw on history of substance use disorder treatment and severity of the addiction, psychiatric comorbidity, and social disintegration. Few treatments and low severity lead to LOC 1: Outpatient advice; more treatments or higher severity escalate to LOC 2: Outpatient treatment, LOC 3: Day/Residential, and LOC 4: Care.

CoTracker Pipeline. Stereo videos are time-synchronized, used to compute calibration matrices, and trimmed for each trial; SPIGA then places facial landmarks on the left (L) and right (R) videos. The CoTracker Transformer Model takes the trimmed L and R videos and SPIGA landmarks to track lip points across frames, and the L and R results are used to compute 3D coordinates and then calculate 3D lip aperture.

The workflow of crop water footprint simulations in this study. It runs from input data collection (climate, soil, crop, management, and distribution data) to crop modelling of crop yield and green and blue crop water use in each grid cell. Post processing then scales national harvested area and simulated yields to FAOSTAT and estimates water footprints per grid cell and country, ending in water footprints of 175 crops in 1990–2019.

Flow chart of cumulative hemostasis rate at different time intervals. It runs from 24-hour hemostasis (22/25, 88%) to 72-hour hemostasis (17/19, 89%), 7-day hemostasis (11/19, 58%), and 14-day hemostasis (9/18, 50%). Side branches show that 6 patients died after 24-hour hemostasis (respiratory failure 2, progression of cancer 4) and 1 patient died of perforated ulcer after 7-day hemostasis.

Flow diagram of the patients included in the study. Hematology patients at West China Hospital with suspected infection who underwent plasma mNGS from October 2020 to July 2023 were enrolled (n = 183 tests). After excluding incomplete information, no hematologic disease, and repeat tests, 153 patients were included, with all CMT results within 3 and 7 days of mNGS collected. These lead to mNGS detection (positive rate 88.24%) and CMT detection (3-day and 7-day positive rates).

PRISMA flow diagram for final article inclusion. Two parallel arms, articles from previous reviews (Day et al., Hoffman et al., Kudret et al.) and from databases (Web of Science, PsycINFO, ProQuest), each remove duplicates, assess eligibility for title review, exclude articles after title & abstract review, and review full texts for eligibility. The arms then merge, removing further duplicates and excluded articles (for example, self-monitoring or leadership not measured), leaving 51 articles included in review.

Preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) flow diagram. In identification, 944 records are identified from databases. In screening, 908 records are excluded and 36 are screened, and 18 full-text articles are excluded with reasons such as no outcome reported for population of interest, no aTSA patients, and no full-text. The included stage ends with 18 studies included in qualitative synthesis.

Enrollment and analysis of patients. Of 3,309 patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) at Seoul National University Hospital (SNUH) between January 2005 and December 2010, 3,015 did not have acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), leaving 294 eligible. After 112 were excluded (not intubated within 24 hours of ICU transfer, ICU stays less than 48 hours, or transferred from outside hospitals), 182 were finally analyzed.

Study flowchart of SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR tests. From 13,096 PCR tests from 812 HCT or CAR T-cell therapy patients, 207 tests are excluded, leaving 12,889 tests from 812 patients. These split into symptomatic test indication (17 positive tests) and asymptomatic test indication, which divides into outpatient weekly surveillance, inpatient surveillance, and pre-procedural/pre-admission testing (32, 1, and 3 positive tests). The asymptomatic positive tests lead to chart review completed.

Flowchart of the stages of cross-cultural adaptation. It starts with Planning the process phases, followed by two parallel translations (Translation 1 and Translation 2) that are combined in a Synthesis. The synthesis then undergoes two parallel back translations (Back Translation 1 and Back Translation 2), which both lead to the Expert Committee. The flow continues to the Pre-test (Pilot) and ends with the Committee of judges.

PRISMA 2020 flow diagram with Identification, Screening, and Included phases. Records identified from databases (n = 350), registers (n = 0), and reference list screening (n = 30) lose 80 duplicates, leaving 300 records screened, of which 220 are excluded at the title/abstract stage. All 80 reports sought are retrieved and assessed for eligibility; those not AI-focused, not on DR/DME, or commentary/non-original data are excluded, and 60 studies are included in the review.

Stepwise procedure for PROMETHEE, drawn as five sequential steps. Step 1 constructs and normalizes the decision matrix, with separate equations for beneficial and non-beneficial criteria; Step 2 applies the preference function Pj(i, i′); Step 3 calculates an overall or aggregated preference π(i, i′) weighted by each criterion's importance Wj. Step 4 calculates the positive and negative outranking flows, and Step 5 ends with the net outranking flow Φ(i) for each alternative.

Flow chart for analyzing the hemodynamic profile according to De Backer. LACTATE splits into > 2 and ≤ 2 mEq/L, each then by ScvO2 (< 70% or ≥ 70%) and PvaCO2 (≤ 6 or > 6 mmHg). High-lactate end points are high CO with dysoxia (anemia), low CO with dysoxia, high CO with dysoxia (sepsis), and microcir. alterations with dysoxia; low-lactate end points are high CO with dysoxia (anemia), low CO without dysoxia, normal, and microcir. alterations without dysoxia.

Timing for tissue processing steps for fresh never frozen human temporal bones, shown as mean time required with range. Time-of-death leads to placement in NS at 4°C after 28 h [12 h - 48 h], which leads to the start of flux testing after 15 h [4 h - 20 h]. A bracket spanning the whole sequence gives an overall time of 43 h [32 h - 63 h].

Decision tree model to predict the likelihood of primary aldosteronism in patients with recent stroke. The root node (Absent, 186 6) splits on AF: AF = N leads to the leaf Absent (179 3), while Y leads to a node Absent (7 3) that splits on DBP. DBP < 83 ends in the leaf Absent (7 0), and DBP >= 83 ends in the leaf Present (0 3).

Block diagram of the PD-Fuzzy-P controller using a decentralize algorithm. The error e.g between q ref. and fed-back q passes through R(-θ) to give e.b, which feeds the PD Fuzzy controller and the P controller; the output u passes through Eq.12, Eq.9, and an integrator to give q, alongside a top view of the three-motor base. The PD Fuzzy controller expands into eH, eV, and eth channels, each with Kp and du/dt-Kd paths into the Horizontal, Vertical, or Rotational Controller.

Flowchart of the research sample analyzed. It starts with 1,323 patients intubated between June 2020 and February 2022, from whom those meeting the exclusion criteria (inadequate medical records, age < 18 years, use of etomidate and others, no induction agent used, loss of follow-up) are removed, leaving 1,117 patients. These are divided into an ETOMIDATE group (563 patients) and a NO ETOMIDATE group (554 patients).

Algorithm flowchart for model construction. Patients aged 15-89 y from MIMICS-III, with lactate, pH, bicarbonate, potassium, calcium, glucose, chloride, and sodium, are split into a Survivors Data Subset and a Nonsurvivors Data Subset of four time windows. These form the EMA 48-72, EMA 24-48, EMA 8-24, and LEMA 0-8 models, each split into testing and training sets, trained with DL, RF, GLM, and evaluated by ROC, specificity, sensitivity & accuracy. LEMA is also applied to earlier testing sets for backcasting.

Study flowchart in line with the STROBE statement for retrospective data collection (January 1, 2020-February 18, 2022). Of 1,326,754 Abruzzo residents assessed for eligibility, 63,673 with a positive SARS-CoV-2 swab before follow-up are excluded, leaving 1,279,694 subjects. After merging the vaccination dataset, subjects branch into unvaccinated, one-dose, two-dose, and three-dose groups, which all converge on merging of the hospitalization and co-pay exemption datasets, ending in Analyses (mean follow-up: 244 days).

Study flow chart comparing endoscopic recurrence in low-risk and high-risk Crohn's disease patients after ileocolonic resection. After exclusions, loss to follow-up, waiting on stoma removal, and still in follow-up, the RAP-CD cohort (n = 260) yields a study population of 213, split into Low risk (n = 93) and High risk (n = 120). In each arm, treatment advice leads to adherence or non adherence, then prophylaxis or no prophylaxis, and, apart from patients with no endoscopy, endoscopic recurrence.

Example flow charts created from reported tissue clearing protocols, with columns Fixation, Pre-treatment, Labeling, Delipidation, Refractive Index Matching, and Organism/Tissue. (A) Successful protocols: PFA, 4% overnight and methanol dehydration branch into four labeling options, each followed by THF, dibenzyl ether, DCM and dibenzyl ether (RI: 1.54), ending in whole brain, mouse whole brain, or mouse cortex section. (B) Not successful protocols: three flows ending in mouse embryo, human brain (via hydrogel embedding or SHIELD), and mouse section of cortex.

Algorithm showing the identification of articles included in the review, across Identification, Screening, and Eligibility phases. Records identified through database searching (n = 428) and through other sources (n = 5) merge into records after duplicates removed (25 meta-analyses, 16 RCT, 7 guidelines), from which 5 records are excluded. The remaining records (21 meta-analyses, 14 RCT, 7 guidelines) lead to 42 full-text articles assessed for eligibility.

Flow chart of the dummy run in two steps. In Step 1, the host institution provides anonymized CT for Scenarios 1-3; 7 institutions plan radiotherapy according to each institution's policies, and DVHs are analyzed based on the reference structure set. This leads to Step 2, where the anonymized CT plus additional information (AI auto-contoured structures, LN boost target volumes, target area definition, OAR dose constraints) goes to the 7 institutions for planning referring to it, again ending with DVH analysis.

Diagram of eligible studies selection procedures across Identification, Screening, Eligibility, and Included phases. Records from electronic databases (n=406), Clinicaltrial.gov, and the Cochrane Central Registry of Controlled Trials are combined; 370 records are excluded after reading the abstract, leaving 146 articles identified for eligibility. After 129 are excluded (not finished, outcomes not interested, not target drugs), 17 trials remain to review, and after 7 more trials are excluded, 10 trials are involved in quantitative analysis.

Trial profile in the form of a Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) diagram. Of 21 patients assessed for eligibility, 16 are excluded (declined, withdrawn prior to randomisation, TIA/cancer, no reply) and 5 are randomised. Randomisation branches into Active treatment (n=4), where all complete 6 M f/up and one is deceased after 6M f/up, and Placebo (n=1), who completes 6 M f/up.

Flowchart of the STL-PCA-BWO-BiLSTM model. Pig price data are decomposed using STL and modeled per component, influencing factors undergo Spearman correlation and PCA, and BWO parameters are initialized. Each iteration calculates Bf and Wf, updates the Beluga whale position in the search phase (Bf > 0.5) or prey phase, computes fitness, and updates again if Wf > Bf, repeating until max iters is reached. The optimal BiLSTM hyperparameters then establish the model, which yields prediction results before the end.

Research flowchart of systems medicine design for human skin aging. Candidate PPIN and GRN networks are combined into a candidate GWGEN, modeled stochastically, and identified with skin microarray data to give real GWGENs in young-, middle-, and elder-stage skin. Principal network projection yields core GWGENs, core signaling pathways for young-to-middle and middle-to-elder aging, the aging molecular mechanism, and essential biomarkers as drug targets. A deep neural network of drug-target interaction with two filters, using BindingDB, ends with two multiple-molecule drugs.

Diagnostic algorithm for soft tissue tumors suspected of EHE. IHC for CAMTA1 and TFE3 gives three branches. CAMTA1+, TFE3- leads directly to diagnosis; for CAMTA1-, TFE3+, a clinically and histologically typical case leads to diagnosis, while an atypical case goes to TFE3 FISH (positive to diagnosis, negative/atypical signal to NGS). CAMTA1-, TFE3- goes to TFE3/CAMTA1 FISH, where TFE3- or CAMTA1-rearrangement leads to diagnosis and both negative leads to NGS.

Retrospective workflow of thyroid nodule (C-TIRADS 4) contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) examinations collected from September 2019 to February 2023 (n=571). Exclusions (missing pathology or Bethesda I/III/IV results, CEUS without "flash" procedure, macro-calcification in 2D-US, poor image quality or incomplete clinical data) leave 313 eligible patients (malignant=203, benign=110). These are split at a ratio of 9:1 into a training cohort (n=282) and a test cohort (n=31).

Flow chart of TB/HIV patients from Minsk, Belarus, with Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) cultures and drug-susceptibility testing (DST). Of 62 HIV-positive patients with TB, 55 are culture positive, 34 samples are sent to Copenhagen, and 30 remain available after unidentified PIDs. Samples undergo phenotypic DST and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) in parallel; culture failures and resistance-detected cultures go to line probe assay (LPA), while no-resistance cultures stop. WGS and LPA each end in results available or failed.

Path model for the quantification of resilience metrics. The latent trait Residual Cognitive Resilience has three indicators: Residual (PACC|Amyloid), Residual (Memory|Amyloid), and Residual (Executive|Amyloid). Combined Resilience is a second-order latent trait whose indicators are Residual Cognitive Resilience and Educational Attainment. PACC = Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite.

Flow of decision-making on cases to simulate, starting from whether once-through design with horizontal serpentine tubes and vertical headers is valid for super- and subcritical sandTES heat exchangers. Five questions follow in sequence, each answered by simulations and a conclusion: super- versus subcritical and heating versus cooling differences (both relevant), part-load unbalance (increases), header design modifications (Yes), start-up and shut-down (shut-down might need a thorough concept), and scale-up height (sufficient for sandTES technology).

Fontan-associated liver disease algorithm based on the liver stiffness measurement by transient elastography and elapsed time since Fontan surgery. The algorithm rules-out Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) when the liver stiffness measurement by transient elastography (FibroScan®) is < 15 kPa, and rules-in FALD when it is ≥ 25 kPa. For patients in the “grey area” of 15-25 kPa, elapsed time since Fontan surgery is used. When the time elapsed is ≤ 10 years, FALD is ruled-out, and when it is > 10 years, it is ruled-in. Schematic overview of the study design and analysis pipeline. Image time series from Scan 1 (S1) and the repeated Scan 2 (S2) were retrospectively truncated to 15, 30, 45, and 55 s. The 55‐s dataset was evaluated twice to account for potential nondeterministic registration effects, with the first analysis defined as the ground truth (GT). All chunks were processed with the PREFUL pipeline using two registration variants (Forsberg and ANTs). Resulting parameters were compared to the 55‐s GT using global and regional measures (black arrows) and between Ex. 1 and Ex. 2 using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC, black dashed lines). The 55‐s datasets were additionally used to directly compare registration methods (red arrows). Finally, all results were correlated with pulmonary function test measures (black dashed arrows).

Algorithm workflow. The events (in reciprocal-space coordinates) are histogrammed to a regular grid. Detector positions, lattice parameters and sample orientations are used to calculate the trajectories in reciprocal space for each detector. The intersections of these trajectories with the given grid, together with counting time and solid-angle information, are used to calculate the statistical weights. Finally, the histogrammed event data are divided by the normalization (the weight) histogram, to obtain the normalized intensity histogram.
